prompt:
mdtable.py in the workspace is a rough draft of a markdown table formatter (Python standard library only). Finish it so it follows every rule below. It must provide two functions: format_table(text) formats one table given as text and returns the formatted table as a string, and format_document(text) formats every table inside a markdown document and returns the whole document. test_basic.py has one simple test; more tests for each numbered rule will be run.

A table has a header row, a delimiter row and zero or more body rows.

1. Splitting. Each row is split into cells at pipes. A leading and a trailing pipe are optional and are not cells. A pipe is escaped when it is preceded by an odd number of backslashes: it does not split and stays in the cell exactly as written (`\|`). A pipe preceded by an even number of backslashes (including none) splits. Backticks have no special meaning. Cell text is trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace; whitespace inside a cell is kept as is.
2. Delimiter row. Each delimiter cell must match `:?-+:?` after trimming. `:--` is left, `--:` is right, `:-:` is center, `---` is no alignment. In the output the delimiter cell has the width of its column and is written as `:` followed by dashes for left, dashes followed by `:` for right, `:` dashes `:` for center, and only dashes for none. Its own width in the input does not matter.
3. Column width. The width of a column is the widest display width of its cells, header included, but at least 3.
4. Display width. A character has width 2 when unicodedata.east_asian_width gives W or F, width 0 when unicodedata.combining is not 0 or its category is Mn, Me or Cf, and width 1 otherwise. The width of a cell is the sum over its characters, counted on the text as written (so `\|` counts 2).
5. Alignment. Header cells and body cells are padded with spaces to the column width according to the column's alignment: left and none put the spaces after the text, right puts them before, center splits them and gives the extra space to the right side when the number is odd.
6. Ragged rows. The number of columns is the number of header cells. A body row with fewer cells is filled up with empty cells, a body row with more cells loses the extra cells. A delimiter row with fewer cells gives no alignment to the missing columns and extra delimiter cells are ignored.
7. Empty cells. A cell that is empty after trimming stays empty: it is written as spaces up to the column width, with no placeholder text. A row of only empty cells is still a row.
8. Rows are written as `| ` + the cells joined by ` | ` + ` |`, and the delimiter row the same way. Lines are joined with `\n`, with no trailing newline and no trailing spaces. format_table ignores blank lines in its input and accepts `\r\n` line endings and indentation. When the text has fewer than two non blank lines it raises ValueError("not a table: needs a header and a delimiter row"). When the second line is not a valid delimiter row (some cell does not match the pattern, or there are no cells) it raises ValueError("not a table: bad delimiter row").
9. Idempotence. format_table(format_table(x)) equals format_table(x) for every valid table, including tables with escaped pipes, wide characters, empty cells and ragged rows, and every line of the output has the same display width.
10. format_document. A table starts at a line that has an unescaped pipe and is immediately followed by a valid delimiter row that also has at least one pipe (so `Heading` over `---` is not a table). The table continues over the following lines as long as they are not blank and contain an unescaped pipe. A line indented with 4 or more spaces or a tab does not start a table. Tables inside fenced code blocks are left exactly as they are; a fence starts with 3 or more backticks or tildes (up to 3 spaces of indentation) and ends at a line with only a marker of the same character and at least the same length. A block whose delimiter row is not valid is left unchanged and raises nothing. Every other character of the document stays exactly as it was, including line endings (a document that contains CRLF is written back with CRLF throughout) and whether it ends with a newline. The formatted table lines are not indented.
11. Inner spacing and cleanup. Whitespace inside a cell is never collapsed, the output never contains `\r`, and an input that ends in a newline gives the same result as one that does not.

Check your work with your own tests, since the numbered rules will be checked one by one.
